chapter: England, Paris and memories of Kansas City and Harlem
title: Moe Gale sends her to England to break the union ban
summary: After Glaser's bookings, Moe Gale sent her to England to break a thirty-year union ban; she played with Ted Heath and others and was held over eleven months.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: After you finished in Cafe Society, where did you go then?

I had been in that one place so long till I went in and out of the city. Glaser booked me. We never could get along but I love Glaser. He's somebody that I always cared for and I think he was very fond of me. I went to him and he booked me on a lot of things. I worked for him for quite a while and then Moe Gale decided that they wanted to break a ban in Europe, a ban of 30 years, so they said the best person to send over there is Mary Lou because the musicians like her. That meant that if I played with all the musicians in England, that the ban would be automatically broken. It seems that 30 years previously to that, English musicians came here to America. Something happened they weren't allowed to play, so that when any American musicians went to England they did the same thing. It was some kind of a battle between the unions. So Moe Gale got together and they sent me to England to break this ban of 30 years. So I played with Ted Heath
and all the big bands there, every musician in England. That automatically broke the ban. The next person that came over was - the Jazz at the Philharmonic, what was his name - ?
When you played with Heath were you playing concerts?
Yes, I played at the Palladium with Heath and all bands there, Johnny Dankworth - just all the musicians I worked with there.
How long did you stay in England?

Well, I went there for 9 days and I was held over 6 months. I stayed in England 11 months. I didn't have any clothes or anything. I had to send back to the store and have my saleslady send me a couple of dresses, but they fitted; she knew what I liked. From there I went to Paris.
